title: US advance retail sales monthly change, June 2026
question: What will the U.S. Census Bureau first print for the seasonally adjusted advance monthly percent change in retail and food services sales, total NAICS 44X72, from May 2026 to June 2026?
resolutionSource: U.S. Census Bureau Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services release
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first Census Bureau Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services PDF released for June 2026, scheduled for July 16, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET, Table 2, Retail & food services total, percent change for June 2026 Advance from May 2026, seasonally adjusted and not price-adjusted. Use the printed value rounded to 0.1 percentage point and ignore all later revisions or benchmark updates.

historicalContext.label: 2025-05 current-vintage adjusted from 2025-04, computed from Table 1 levels

drivers: May advance print was strong at +0.9% after revised April +0.4%
Total retail and food services sales level was $763.7 billion in May 2026
Recent monthly changes show high noise with a small positive central tendency
Judgmental momentum from the total-series prints modestly offsets mean reversion risk
First-print advance estimate is based on an early subsample and is revision-prone

reasoning.text: June 2026 advance retail sales monthly-change forecast

Framing and exact resolver: this target is Census MARTS/Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services, total retail and food services NAICS 44X72, seasonally adjusted and not adjusted for price changes. The first-print value is the Table 2 percent change for June 2026 Advance from May 2026, not the later MRTS preliminary revision.

reasoning.call: Checked Census Monthly Retail Trade release schedule and Economic Indicator calendar for June 2026 Advance Monthly Retail Trade Report.
reasoning.result: Census lists the Advance Monthly Retail Trade Report data month June 2026 for release on July 16, 2026 at 8:30 am; the calendar separately lists Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services on July 16, 2026 at 8:30 AM for period June 2026.

reasoning.call: Read the May 2026 Census advance retail sales release PDF text and headline values.
reasoning.result: The May 2026 release says adjusted retail and food services sales were $763.7 billion, up 0.9 percent from April 2026 and up 6.9 percent from May 2025; March 2026 to April 2026 was revised from +0.5 percent to +0.4 percent.

reasoning.call: Read Census Table 1 and Table 2 for recent total retail and food services adjusted values.
reasoning.result: Table 1 adjusted total retail and food services levels were 763705 million for May 2026, 757036 million for April 2026, 754013 million for March 2026, 714568 million for May 2025, and 722442 million for April 2025; Table 2 prints May 2026 from April 2026 at +0.9 and April 2026 from March 2026 at +0.4.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: using recent Census total retail and food services monthly-change evidence available in the release, the fetched values are +0.9, +0.4, and the current-vintage Table 1 April-to-May 2025 adjusted-level change of roughly -1.1. That limited reference class centers near zero but has material month-to-month volatility.

Variant consistency: the target and the direct anchors are Census Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services total retail and food services, seasonally adjusted, not price-adjusted. The 2025 comparison is computed from current-vintage adjusted Table 1 levels, so it is used only as a fallback volatility/context point, not as a verified first-print advance Table 2 observation.

Prior/update/interval: persistence/base-rate prior uses available recent monthly changes [0.9, 0.4, -1.1], mean = (0.9 + 0.4 - 1.1)/3 = 0.07. Current-release adjustment adds +0.20 as a judgmental momentum update from the total-series +0.9 May print after +0.4 April, with no separate category breadth adjustment, giving point about 0.27 rounded to 0.3. For the interval, this 3-point sample is a fallback heuristic because a longer first-print sample was not fetched; sample sigma = 1.04 from [0.9, 0.4, -1.1], 1.28*sigma = 1.33, so 0.3 +/- 1.3 gives about -1.0 to 1.6, a reasonable 80% band for a noisy advance nominal monthly-change print.

Upside risk: unusually strong nominal spending across high-weight retail categories or a large seasonal-adjustment surprise would land above the interval. Downside risk: a broad June reversal after May's strong total print would land below the interval. A shock large enough to move the total monthly change beyond roughly +/-1.3 percentage points from the point forecast is the main outside the interval scenario.

Review disposition: accepted the critique to remove unsupported ex-gas, ex-auto, gasoline, and motor-vehicle update claims; accepted the critique to label the 3-point sigma as a fallback heuristic; accepted the clarification that the 2025 value is current-vintage Table 1 context rather than a verified first-print Table 2 advance value.
